note: F1: house rule - an Eduqas/WJEC lesson must not name the board in student-facing prose.

find: Examiners reward this kind of nuanced, balanced analysis throughout your answer.
replace: Keep that balance of strength and limitation running through the whole answer.
note: F2: removes an invented claim about what examiners reward; keeps the advice.

find: Example: 50 million PET drinks bottles produced per day worldwide.
replace: Example: over a billion PET drinks bottles are made worldwide every day.
note: F3: 480 billion bottles sold in 2017 is about 1.3 billion a day, so the old figure was about 26 times too low.

find: PHA requires specific anaerobic soil or marine conditions
replace: PHA needs the right soil or marine conditions
note: F4: PHA does not need anaerobic conditions; soil and seawater are aerobic, and Lesson 2 says the same.

find: uPVC is the most commonly extruded polymer (window and door frames), but polyethylene, polypropylene and nylon are also widely extruded.
replace: uPVC is widely extruded (window and door frames), and polyethylene, polypropylene and nylon are also extruded in large quantities.
note: F5: polyethylene is made in about three times the tonnage of PVC and most of it is extruded, so uPVC is not the most extruded polymer.

expect: Name the shaping process used for thermosetting polymers such as urea formaldehyde.
value: Name the shaping process used for thermosetting polymers such as urea formaldehyde, and briefly describe how it works.
note: F6: the question was set at 2 marks but only asked for a name, so a correct two-word answer could reach 1 mark. The stem now asks for the description the mark scheme pays for.

find: used for PVC pipes, boat hulls and chemical storage tanks
replace: used for PVC pipes, pond liners and chemical storage tanks
note: F7: boat hulls are polyester resin (a thermoset) in Lesson 1 and cannot be welded; pond liners are a true hot gas welding product.
